articles.title: ARMRA Made A Colostrum Soda. Will Anyone Buy A Second 12-Pack?
articles.summary: ARMRA's new colostrum soda turns a trendy supplement into a $4 functional beverage. Here's how it tastes—and whether it can become a real category.
articles.body:
It was probably only a matter of time before someone put colostrum in a can and gave it bubbles.

Colostrum, the nutrient-rich first milk mammals produce after giving birth, is often touted as "liquid gold" for the concentrated antibodies, proteins and other nutrients it delivers to newborns. Since drinking human breast milk as adults presumably felt too weird even for the wellness-obsessed— taint tanning notwithstanding—supplement makers did the next most logical thing: turned to cows.

Bovine colostrum has spent the past few years migrating from bodybuilding circles into expensive jars, single-serve sticks, and GRWM social media morning routines. Now, ARMRA , a physician-founded supplement brand best known for its bovine colostrum powders, has put it in a 12-ounce can and suggested we make it our afternoon treat.

Introduced in late April 2026, ARMRA Colostrum Soda comes in four flavors: Spicy Lime, Huckleberry, Pomelo Basil and Pear Ginger. Each sugar-free can contains one gram of ARMRA's bovine colostrum concentrate and retails for $3.99 at Sprouts ; a 12-pack is $49.99 online before shipping. ARMRA isn't asking customers to trade their jar of powder for a can of pop. The brand wants them to make room for both.

This can be a lucrative proposition. Functional soda has already shown that an ingredient story can create a new fridge favorite. PepsiCo paid $1.95 billion for prebiotic soda brand Poppi in 2025. ARMRA's bet is that colostrum can follow this perpetual path to personal optimization and go from niche supplement to cold, convenient beverage.

Asked what ARMRA expected the soda to compete with in the refrigerator, Sarah Rahal, MD, ARMRA's founder and CEO, is blunt: "Nothing, and that's not a dodge." The company's jarred colostrum powders fit the parts of the day that repeat—like a skincare routine or a morning cold plunge—while the can is meant for everything in between. "Discipline already had a product," she says. "Desire didn't."

It is tidy brand language, but it helps explain the opportunity: ARMRA is not merely adding colostrum to soda. It wants consumers to see colostrum itself as something they might crave, like an ice-cold Diet Coke.

This premise only works if the beverage in the can is enjoyable, with or without the liquid gold promise.

Out of curiosity—presumably because I was formula fed as a baby and wanted to know what I'd missed—I tried the sodas myself. The Pomelo Basil was easily my favorite; the basil note was satisfyingly assertive, while the pomelo tasted fresh and true rather than artificial. It was crisp and tart, like a refreshing Italian soda. The Pear Ginger was milder, but the ginger brought a fun hit of heat. Spicy Lime should appeal to fans of Mountain Dew or spicy margaritas, or, ideally, both. Huckleberry gave me the most pause. I'm not sure what a huckleberry is supposed to taste like, but I'm fairly certain I've never encountered a fruit that tastes like this soda. All four were properly fizzy, with a subtle creaminess to the texture.

articles.title: VIDEO: Angelo State soccer team will start new chapter under head coach Mike Erwin
articles.summary: SAN ANGELO, Texas (Concho Valley Homepage) — The Angelo State University soccer team opens a new era under first-year head coach Mike Erwin at home Thursday...
articles.body:
SAN ANGELO, Texas ( Concho Valley Homepage ) — The Angelo State University soccer team opens a new era under first-year head coach Mike Erwin at home Thursday against MSU Denver.

The Belles have nine returners back and 13 newcomers.

In Travis McCorkle's final season last year, ASU finished 9-5-5 overall and 8-3-3 in the Lone Star Conference. The Belles were eliminated in the first round of the LSC Tourney.

ASU has been picked to finish seventh in conference in the LSC Preseason Poll.

The season opener against MSU Denver is scheduled for 1 p.m. Thursday at the LeGrand Soccer Complex.

Click on the video above to hear what the Belles' new braintrust had to say earlier this week at Media Day.

articles.title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson gets update after injury scare
articles.summary: What's the latest on the health status of Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson, who left Monday's practice early with an injury?
articles.body:
New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson suffered an injury scare during Monday's practice, when he reportedly slipped on the turf during a cut.

He left the practice session early after what looked like an ankle injury.

On Tuesday, Boston Globe Sports' Christopher Price revealed that Henderson suffered a right ankle injury and had "precautionary tests" done. However, the good news for the Patriots is that the second-year running back is "walking and moving fine."

"According to a league source, TreVeyon Henderson is getting some "precautionary tests" done on his right ankle, but is walking and moving fine. Described as a lower ankle issue he sustained after slipping on the turf during practice Monday," Price wrote.

According to a league source, TreVeyon Henderson is getting some ”precautionary tests” done on his right ankle, but is walking and moving fine. Described as a lower ankle issue he sustained after slipping on the turf during practice Monday. — Christopher Price (@cpriceglobe) August 25, 2026

According to a league source, TreVeyon Henderson is getting some ”precautionary tests” done on his right ankle, but is walking and moving fine. Described as a lower ankle issue he sustained after slipping on the turf during practice Monday.

When speaking with media members, Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf confirmed that Henderson would not practice on Tuesday .

That isn't exactly surprising with the Patriots wanting to ensure one of their best offensive weapons is healthy and ready for the regular season. The team will go on the road for their preseason finale against the Cleveland Browns on Thursday, which is less than two weeks before their regular season opener against the Seattle Seahawks .

articles.title: Trump administration issues pause on visa appointments for applicants worldwide
articles.summary: By Kanishka Singh WASHINGTON, Aug 25 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump's administration has issued a pause on visa appointments for applicants around the wo...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Aug 25 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump's administration has issued a pause on visa appointments for applicants around the world during an ongoing ‌immigration crackdown by the U.S. government in the Republican leader's second term ‌in the White House.

A U.S. State Department spokesperson said on Tuesday that it launched a global training initiative ​at all U.S. embassies and consulates worldwide and that appointments for visa services will be adjusted to accommodate the training.

Trump has pursued an aggressive deportation drive and immigration crackdown that includes revocations of visas and green cards and rejection of applications over a. range of reasons ‌like political opinions and pro-Palestinian ⁠protests against U.S. ally Israel's assault on Gaza.

He says the crackdown aims to improve domestic security.

The crackdown has faced some legal setbacks. ⁠A U.S. judge on Friday struck down a Trump administration policy suspending the issuance of immigrant visas to applicants from 75 countries, saying that the policy exceeded Secretary of State Marco ​Rubio's statutory ​authority.

The State Department did not specify details ​on the training and its timeline, ‌beyond saying the training aimed to help consular officers screen out applicants deemed likely to become dependent on U.S. public benefits and to ensure evaluation of visa applicants "comprehensively and consistently."

The pause on visa appointments was reported earlier by the Financial Times, which said immigrant visa applicants with scheduled interviews at U.S. embassies and consulates have received emails that ‌their appointments were being rescheduled and that they ​would receive future notice of a new date.

Trump's immigration ​crackdown has been widely condemned ​by human rights groups as being discriminatory and in violation of free ‌speech and due process rights. Rights ​groups also say the ​crackdown has created an unsafe environment in the U.S., especially for ethnic minorities who have raised concerns about racial profiling.

While Trump campaigned in 2024 on a ​platform of stopping illegal immigration, ‌his administration has also made legal immigration more difficult - or example, by imposing ​new and expensive fees for applicants of certain work visas.

(Reporting by Kanishka ​Singh in Washington; Editing by Stephen Coates)
